### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 713545fd118fa9839795394bc01c376018c97826` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37c19c7832ea92aced51781ccf87da04d253b1c3` — the merge of head `b2e82158b5ebe7f2f06a5f2d318930353483ac6b` into base `713545fd118fa9839795394bc01c376018c97826`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37c19c7832ea92aced51781ccf87da04d253b1c3 && git checkout 37c19c7832ea92aced51781ccf87da04d253b1c3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 713545fd118fa9839795394bc01c376018c97826 b2e82158b5ebe7f2f06a5f2d318930353483ac6b && git checkout -B drift-repro 713545fd118fa9839795394bc01c376018c97826 && git merge --no-ff b2e82158b5ebe7f2f06a5f2d318930353483ac6b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 713545fd118fa9839795394bc01c376018c97826
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK, held on one reading question for the seat** at head `ca5b93e15b327fcf6e7c5bf4a8e9831d83b60ceb` (Fixes #35823, route narrowed by the seat in 7065273884). Full read of `origin/main...ca5b93e15b` (4 files, +176/−2).

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 36138` at ca5b93e15b:
  - Shape: draft against `main`, first line `Fixes #35823`, and no closing keyword binds another card.
  - Declarations: `fix(metadata-protocol)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
  - Floors: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are success, and `mergeable_state` is clean.
  - Check-runs: all success or expected skip, 0 failing, 0 pending.
- One flag, answered: dogfood. The narrowing arm's full battery is pinned at this head in 7066311396 (483 files passed / 3 skipped, 4101 tests passed / 68 skipped, command exit 0). That is the evidence the `!` needs.
- Changeset `35823-unmanaged-derived-namespace-mismatch.md` names `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (the only published package touched), carries the BREAKING sentence, and the declaration lines match the body.
- Docs: `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx` gains the refusal row, so no published page is left false by this round.

**What the code does.** `derivedNamespaceMismatch` runs only when the body declares no `namespace` and a `targetNamespace` is given. A name that starts with `<derived>_` passes. A name with no `_` passes ("bare"). **Every other name is refused**, and the refusal treats the text before the FIRST `_` as "the prefix it carries".

**R1 (held for the seat; I do not decide it).** Whether a multi-segment name without the derived prefix counts as "carrying another prefix" (refused) or as "a name that lacks the package's prefix" (renamed in front).
- At this head such a name is refused. The test `names every contradicting object, and only those` has `asset_lifecycle_b_owner` passing only because it starts with the derived namespace. A name like `purchase_order` or `asset_owner` in a namespace-less package is now refused on the rename path, where main renamed it to `<target>_purchase_order`.
- ADR-0048 §3.5 (2026-11-07 note): "a name that lacks the package's prefix takes it in front". The seat's route (7065273884) keeps that for "a bare name". The code defines "bare" as one segment only. The card's Done-when speaks of "the names' **common** prefix" differing from the derived namespace, which is a different test again (one prefix shared by the names, not a per-name first segment).
- The code cannot tell `purchase_order` (a two-word short name, no prefix) from `demoasset_site` (a real prefix). Which reading holds changes what a customer's install does, and it reads an ADR, so per common.md it goes to the seat. Asked there.

**R2 (after R1 is answered).** Pin the answered reading with a test on a multi-segment name that lacks the derived prefix and is not a real foreign prefix (for example `purchase_order`): refused or renamed, whichever the seat rules. If the ruling is "renamed", the refusal needs a narrower trigger (for example the common-prefix test the card names), and the changeset's "A bare object name (`asset`, no prefix at all)" sentence and the JSDoc change with it.

**N1 (nit, non-blocking).** The hint `namespace: '${carried}'` takes the text before the first `_`. Namespaces may themselves hold `_` (the derived one here is `asset_lifecycle_b`), so for a real prefix `demo_asset` on `demo_asset_site` the sentence suggests `namespace: 'demo'`. The "if that is the prefix" hedge keeps it from being false, but naming the whole name and asking for the prefix it carries would not mislead.

**Not findings.** Refusal tests assert status and code (`[400, 'INVALID_REQUEST']`) and `details.refused`. The controls pin: bare `asset` renamed, derived-prefix names renamed, a declared `namespace` unchanged, the no-rename path unchanged, and the verb refusing before any write. The declared-namespace path (`declaredNamespace !== undefined`) is untouched, as the Done-when asks.

**Next.** The seat answers R1. Then the dev round adds R2's pin (and the narrower trigger if the ruling needs it), and I read only that delta.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 36138` at b2e82158b5:
  - Declarations unchanged: `fix(metadata-protocol)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
  - Floors: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are success.
  - Check-runs: 44 success, 17 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.

- The changeset still names `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.
- Flag answered: dogfood. The full battery at this head is pinned in 7067263519 (483 files passed / 3 skipped, 4101 tests passed / 68 skipped, command exit 0).
- The merge: `git diff a7b30626ba b2e82158b5` on the four PR paths is empty. The PR's net diff is still those four files.

**R1, against the seat reading.** The per-name check is gone. `derivedNamespaceContradiction` refuses only when all of these hold:
- the body declares no `namespace`;
- a rename is asked for;
- there are two or more objects;
- no object carries the derived prefix;
- every object name has the same first segment, and that segment is not the derived namespace.

Otherwise ADR-0048 §3.5's rename applies, as on main.
- **Object names only, not every item name.** This narrows the seat's "every item name" in the safe direction: views such as `demoasset_asset_all` and planner-named translation items would otherwise blur the signal. The JSDoc gives that reason, and contract delta PASS 7066464020 covers it.
- **The "no object carries the derived prefix" guard is load-bearing, and it is pinned.** A derived namespace can hold `_`, as `asset_lifecycle_b` does. So `asset_lifecycle_b_asset` + `asset_lifecycle_b_site` share the first segment `asset`, and without the guard they would be refused. The verb-level control installs exactly those two names and expects them renamed, so it goes red without the guard.
- **Accepted consequence of the seat reading.** Two objects sharing a short first word (`purchase_order`, `purchase_item`) are refused the same way as `demoasset_*`. The changeset and the docs row say so, and declaring `namespace` clears it.

**R2 pins, all present.**
- `purchase_order` alone is renamed to `trialdemoasset_purchase_order`, and so is `purchase_order` beside `asset_owner`.
- Bare `asset` + `site` are renamed.
- A single-object package is not refused, even `demoasset_asset`.
- `demoasset_asset` + `demoasset_site` on the derived path are refused at `[400, 'INVALID_REQUEST']`, one `details.refused` entry each, naming `derived from its id as 'asset_lifecycle_b'`, `begins 'demoasset_'` and the missing key.
- The verb refuses before any write: no write, no package, no `sys_metadata` row.
- A declared `namespace`, matching or not, renames as before.
- Without a rename the plan does not ask.
- Ablation (7067263519): with the common-prefix refusal made a no-op, 2 tests go red; with the declared-namespace gate forced open, 1 goes red. Both were restored by hash.

**N1 fixed.** The remedy now reads "Declare `namespace` on the package, the prefix its object names carry". It no longer suggests a value cut at the first `_`.

**Docs and changeset.** The `install-modes.mdx` row and the changeset paragraphs, read sentence by sentence, match the code: the two-or-more condition, the common first word, no derived prefix, each object named, and a declared namespace unchanged "whatever its names look like". The ADR-0087 comment is updated to the new trigger.

**Not findings.**
- The contradiction refusal is now thrown before the per-item loop, so it is not merged with other per-item refusals in one `details.refused`. That is acceptable: it answers before the base exists, and the verb test pins the outcome.
- `Fixes` is right. The Done-when's "common prefix … refuses with both named", its test pin, and "present namespace unchanged" are all delivered.
- Contract follow-up #36166 is filed.

**Next.** Landing is the seat's: contract delta PASS 7066464020 and this ACCEPT, both at b2e82158b5.
